chapter: Black Benny, brass bands and bass drum
title: Black Benny's showmanship and bass drum style
summary: He describes Black Benny's side-walking dance style and compares Dave Bailey.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Is there anything else about Black Benny you can tell about his Black Benny?

No, that's about all I just know him. I saw him on the street and he's the second line behind him like the rest of the guys during the day. Yeah. Used to watch him. I imagine that's what started me to play in bass drum, but it's the lack that he ain't play.
Did he look like he was better? Some people say throw his sticks around and do more fancy things. Did he look like he was better than the usual bass drum?

The only thing I saw him throw any sticks around, the only things I see him do when he was playing that side walk he had and that singer in his mouth. That side walk? Yeah, he used to walk more on the side and play his drum, you know, like a horse prancing or something.
He started to dance as long as he did?
Were he two second line steps or anything when he was playing?
Well, just that side slack until you get side walking and play his drum.
Well, you've seen Dave Bailey cut up, huh? You know Dave?
He plays with the Gibson and the Jackson Bears, Benny's playing with these onions.
Oh yeah, I know who you're talking about.
Yeah, I know who you're talking about.
Well, you know, he cuts up so much of the music.
Yeah, well, Benny did that, I never seen him do it.
Yeah, I just wondered if anybody back in those times did he?
No, I never seen him. That's the first guy I ever saw do that. I saw him on a couple of jobs. I played in the same parade with him on the carnival day and I saw him join it.
